description: This dataset reconstructs global water use at monthly, 0.5-degree resolution for 1971 to 2010 in six sectors: irrigation, domestic, electricity generation (cooling of thermal power plants), livestock, mining and manufacturing. Country withdrawals from FAO AQUASTAT, and state estimates from USGS for the United States, were downscaled in space and time with several models; industry was split using GCAM, irrigation consumption comes from four global hydrological models, and consumption in other sectors from consumptive-use efficiencies. It was produced by the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research of the Chinese Academy of Sciences with Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (Huang et al.) and published on Zenodo in February 2018 as per-sector archives of several hundred megabytes under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: values are modelled downscalings, not measurements, and the series ends in 2010. Simulation uses: historical demand on irrigation and public water supply for capacity planning and climate adaptation. Related record: the FAO Global Map of Irrigation Areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas).
